entry.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels. Existing vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception.
entry.summary:
Existing vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception. In this report, we present WeVisOne-VL (WeChat Vision All-in-One), a powerful VLM that unifies object-level and pixel-level perception through structured next-token prediction. It supports multiple visual tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting, enabling localization at any user-specific granularity, from points and boxes to masks and alpha mattes.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds. Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling.
entry.summary:
Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts.

entry.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
entry.summary:
Fine-grained visual understanding requires distinguishing subtle differences in local attributes and spatial relations, yet remains challenging for existing vision-language models. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) offer a new opportunity through generation pathways that preserve rich visual information complementary to understanding. However, existing generation-assisted understanding methods mainly rely on generative supervision or explicit generation and have not systematically explored direct use of native generation-side representations.

entry.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) introduce unique quantization challenges due to their iterative denoising process. In this work, we reveal that quantization sensitivity is both taskand time-dependent, with different downstream tasks exhibiting distinct precision requirements across denoising steps. We further show that these patterns can be predicted without groundtruth labels or task-specific evaluation metrics.

entry.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing. LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks.
entry.summary:
LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that integrates these routing modes within a single LLM policy, jointly learning which mode to use and how to select models within that mode.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary:
Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. To further improve its practicality, recent budget-controllable FF3DGS methods allow the number of Gaussians to be adjusted at inference, so that the output meets a given storage limit or rendering-latency constraint. However, these methods overlook the cost of inference itself: to produce a representation with the target number of Gaussians, they first predict a dense set of Gaussians and then prune or select from it, requiring nearly constant latency and peak memory regardless of the budget.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems. We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated).
entry.summary:
We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated). IQuest-Q1 is developed through a three-stage process: (1) stable and efficient pre-training, combining Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum whose second stage increases the coding-data mixture, preserving a wide stability margin between safe and optimal learning rates; (2) fine-grained mid-training, expanding the data mixture across domains and formats and progressively extending the context; and (3) multi-scaffold with multi-version post-training, combining SFT, domain-specialized RL, and MOPD across various scaffolds to integrate complementary training signals and strengthen agentic coding capabilities. Furthermore, model merging combines different experts and checkpoints from different stages while mitigating conflicts among their parameter updates.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
entry.summary:
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) relies on evaluation feedback to assess progress and guide further research, yet repeatedly running complex benchmarks is costly and slows iteration. Human experts reduce this cost by selecting benchmark subsets or designing compact suites. We ask whether AI agents can automate this design process and introduce EvalResearchBench (ERB), a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
entry.summary:
Video scene graph generation (VidSGG) aims to capture objects and their evolving relationships in videos. This requires accounting for both the persistence of object identities and abrupt changes in relationships. Existing methods aggregate information across frames to exploit temporal context, but an emphasis on consistency can obscure these changes.
